acceptance: All nine gated benchmarks have a recorded SF 1 gate run within tolerance, or a recorded owner decision for those that cannot run.
A mutation probe failed required CI and the run is linked.
The owner approved the runtime budget.
context: Filed 2026-11-20 from the adversarial review of the scale-factor and TPC-DI remediation work (PRs #4298-#4385 and benchbox-site #178-#210).
description:
## Problem
The gate's measuring path (`run_smoke`: `benchbox run` at SF 1 on DuckDB, then sizing the datagen tree) has never run in CI; the job was always skipped. The baseline was produced by calling generator classes directly, a different counting path, so agreement is unproven for tpcdi, write_primitives, transaction_primitives and vector_search, and it is unknown whether each benchmark's power phase passes on DuckDB at SF 1. The 45-minute job timeout and 1500 s per-benchmark timeout have no measurement or owner approval. generator-volume-changes-pass-pr-ci-unchecked-20261112 requires a mutation probe that fails required CI, a measured runtime cost and owner approval of the required check and budget.

## Change
Run the gate for each of the nine benchmarks through `make heavy-run` and record measured bytes against the baseline, wall time and peak memory. Fix any disagreement in the counting path, not the baseline. Then run a mutation probe on a throwaway branch pull request that multiplies one generator's output and confirm `core` fails.

## Decision gates
The owner approves the measured runtime budget and the check being required before #4322 is armed. A benchmark whose power phase cannot pass on DuckDB at SF 1 is reported to the owner, not dropped from the gate silently. The throwaway probe pull request is closed unmerged.

## Verification rubric
Pass: a nine-row table (benchmark, baseline bytes, measured bytes, drift, seconds, peak GiB) with heavy-run log paths; the probe pull request's failing `core` run URL; the owner's budget approval recorded on this item.

## Guardrails
- Any limit, default, threshold or label text is shown to the owner before it is committed.
- The implementer never resolves review threads on its own pull request; the reviewer or the owner does.
- No polling loop around `make pr-arm`, no `--no-verify`, and no stand-in review unless the owner names the PR and head unprompted.
- Heavy work runs only through `make heavy-run` or a lock-taking entry point.
- Status reports state only what merged and what was verified, with the evidence.
